question.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) & ⟹\,v=-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into  the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =-2x\cdot \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-\int (-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & ={-\frac{2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}|}_{0}^{\pi /6}+\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-\frac{2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}|}_{0}^{\pi /6}+{\frac{2}{9}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)|}_{0}^{\pi /6} \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}[\frac{\pi }{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})-0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot 0)] \\  & +\frac{2}{9}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot 0)] \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}[0-0]+\frac{2}{9}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)] \\  & =\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
